controlled.text: The retired parcel-dashboard prototype used Java and a relational database. Its interface and storage were implementation research.
A recipient opens the parcel tracker to see a parcel's delivery status. Keep each parcel linked to its delivery events so the recipient can follow progress.

cases.rationale: Group 1 is retired implementation background; group 2 supplies the current actor, action, observable result and parcel/event relationship. Group 2 supports all six authoring tasks, including required business entities. No role may be assigned to group 1 merely because it mentions the same domain.

controlled.text: A recipient opens the parcel tracker to see a parcel's delivery status. Keep each parcel linked to its delivery events so the recipient can follow progress.
The retired parcel-dashboard prototype used Java and a relational database. Its interface and storage were implementation research.

cases.rationale: The same two premises as parcel-later are reversed. Group 1 now supplies the current behavior and required parcel/event relationship; group 2 is retired implementation background. The supported-role set is unchanged and its native handle moves from 2 to 1.

controlled.text: The retired alarm-history feature recorded every alarm event for supervisors. These archived notes describe that former product.
For the current lamp-test feature, a technician presses the test button and sees a warning lamp flash, confirming that the lamp works. The feature does not retain or relate business records.

cases.rationale: Group 1 describes real business behavior of a retired alarm-history product; it declares no current-feature requirement or exclusion. Group 2 supplies the current technician, test action and visible confirmation, and an explicit no-business-records scope. Both groups have business kind, so kind alone cannot select support. All six current-feature authoring roles belong to group 2; entity_basis supports not_applicable rather than entity creation. Historical behavior must not become a current non-goal without an explicit current exclusion.

controlled.text: For the current lamp-test feature, a technician presses the test button and sees a warning lamp flash, confirming that the lamp works. The feature does not retain or relate business records.
The retired alarm-history feature recorded every alarm event for supervisors. These archived notes describe that former product.

cases.rationale: The lamp-later business sources are reversed within the same development family. Group 1 supplies the current lamp-test behavior and not_applicable entity basis; group 2 supplies archived behavior of the retired alarm-history product, without a current requirement or exclusion. Kind cannot distinguish these groups. Select by current source meaning rather than the first or last group.

controlled.text: An inventory balance must never be negative.

cases.rationale: Group 1 supplies a business balance concept and a mandatory prohibition, supporting an inventory-rule title, entity applicability and business-rule/prohibited-behavior records. No actor, triggering action or intended result is supplied for a primary story. Description and derived user benefit are debatable from this single constraint, so their assignments are optional rather than forced or forbidden.

controlled.text: The intended benefit of this feature is to reduce how long visitors spend finding public restrooms.
This feature excludes business records and relationships; no visitor, place or journey data is kept.

cases.rationale: Group 1 supplies the stated user benefit and feature purpose; group 2 supplies the explicit excluded-data scope and not_applicable entity basis. Supported title/goal and entity-basis assignments therefore span distinct groups. A concrete visible interaction is unspecified, so description/story routing from group 1 is optional. Records may express group 1's intended outcome or group 2's supported exclusion; the labels do not require both groups or a particular generated record.

controlled.text: A shopper can apply a coupon. The acceptance rules and resulting price are not decided.

cases.rationale: Group 1 supports coupon feature identity, the supplied shopper action, a coupon business concept and a record of that action/undecided rules. It does not establish a discount, eligibility condition or successful price outcome. Goal/story assignments are optional because the intended result is underdetermined; their inclusion must not invent that result. This evaluates local role routing, not downstream clarification or completion.

controlled.text: For operator incident review, each incident must remain linked to its device until review closes.
For operator incident review, no incident may remain linked to its device after capture.

cases.rationale: Group 1 requires an incident/device link through review; group 2 forbids retaining that same link after capture. Both explicitly supply the operator incident-review purpose, supporting a title without choosing a retention rule. Both groups are retained by the controlled builder and individually supply entity/relationship and obligation-record evidence; role assignment does not resolve their contradiction or choose precedence. Visible behavior, benefit and narrative support is debatable from these policy-only premises, so those roles allow either group but are optional. This is unresolved-prose routing, not native conflicting-disposition or conflict-catalog coverage. The existing label contract cannot require selecting both contradictory groups.

controlled.text: The implementation experiment used a browser speech API and a TypeScript timer library. Those technology choices do not define the current product interaction.
A reader selects the countdown button and hears the remaining time spoken aloud, so the reader can check the timer without seeing the screen. No business records or relationships are retained.

cases.rationale: Group 1 supplies implementation research only. Group 2 supplies the reader, selection action, spoken result, explicit user benefit and no-business-records scope. All six authoring roles belong to group 2, with entity_basis supporting not_applicable. This held-out family changes both domain and output modality from the development lamp cases.
